about.title: Wheatland Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Wheatland is small enough that a death touches nearly everyone. With about 3,725 residents spread along Rt 65, Wheatland Road and Spenceville Road, most families here know each other, and the loss of a parent, spouse or child ripples through the whole community. In 2025, public collision records list 17 injury collisions in Wheatland with 29 people hurt and no traffic deaths, which is a relief, but fatal harm is not limited to the road. Falls, unsafe products, medical mistakes and workplace accidents can also take a life that should not have been lost. California treats wrongful death as a civil matter, separate from any criminal charges, and it gives certain family members the right to seek compensation for funeral costs, the income the person would have provided, and the love and guidance that cannot be replaced. LawProactive exists to make the first step easier. We are not a law firm; we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases and works on contingency, so nothing is owed unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Wheatland Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can quickly sort out which family members have the right to bring the claim so no one is left out.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window shrinks considerably when a government entity is involved. Getting connected soon protects that time.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Every attorney in our network works on contingency, and our connection service is free. Your family can focus on grieving rather than on legal bills.

items.question: My spouse was killed on SR-65 near Wheatland. Does it matter that it is a state highway?
items.answer: It can. If the condition of the roadway or a public vehicle contributed to the crash, a government agency such as Caltrans or Yuba County may be a responsible party. Claims against government entities in California require a formal notice within a much shorter period, generally six months, before the usual two-year wrongful death deadline even applies. Speaking with an attorney early keeps that option open.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that runs on its own track, separate from any criminal prosecution by the district attorney. Your family does not need a conviction to pursue compensation, and waiting for the criminal case could put you close to the filing deadline. An attorney can move forward while the criminal matter is pending.

items.question: What losses can our family recover in a California wrongful death claim?
items.answer: California allows eligible family members to seek funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided over their expected lifetime, and the loss of love, companionship, comfort and guidance. Each family's situation is different, so an attorney will review your specific circumstances rather than quote a figure. Nothing about the outcome can be promised, but the categories of recoverable loss are set by law.
